sentences.en: Programming Throwdown, Episode 101, React.js with Guillermo Rauch.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收看《编程大乱斗》第 101 期，本期嘉宾是 React.js 与 Guillermo Rauch。

sentences.en: Take it away, Jason.
sentences.zh: 交给你了，杰森。

sentences.en: Hey, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: We are here with the CEO of Vercel and a co-creator of Next.js, Guillermo Rauch.
sentences.zh: 今天我们请到了 Vercel 的首席执行官兼 Next.js 的联合创始人吉列尔莫·劳赫（Guillermo Rauch）。

sentences.en: How are you doing today?
sentences.zh: 你今天过得怎么样？

sentences.en: Excellent.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Thanks for being here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你能来。

sentences.en: So I think this is super, super interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这真的、真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: The only thing I've talked a lot about on this show is for people who want to just get into coding, try to build something where you can interact with it and even better, something
sentences.zh: 我在节目里经常谈到的一点是，对于那些刚开始接触编程的人，试着构建一些你可以与之互动的东西，更好的是，

sentences.en: where other people can interact with it.
sentences.zh: 一个其他人也可以与之互动的东西。

sentences.en: You know, that's the way, you know, the hardest part about getting into coding, this is true
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是入门编程最难的部分，

sentences.en: if you're listening and you're a high school student, college student, or if you're, you know, coming to this from another profession, you know, is just keeping motivated, right?
sentences.zh: 无论你是在听节目的高中生、大学生，还是从其他行业转行过来的人，最难的其实就是保持动力，对吧？

sentences.en: And the best way to stay motivated is to have something you can show someone.
sentences.zh: 而保持动力最好的方法，就是做出一个能拿给别人看的东西。

sentences.en: And really, the best way to do that is with the web.
sentences.zh: 说实话，实现这一点的最佳途径就是通过网页。

sentences.en: Um, you know, it's, as someone who's rolled out, you know, desktop apps, I can tell you it's a huge nightmare, a little bit easier on mobile and not that much.
sentences.zh: 作为一个发布过桌面端应用的人，我可以告诉你那简直是个巨大的噩梦，移动端稍微容易一点，但也有限。

sentences.en: Um, but on the web, you know, it's beautiful.
sentences.zh: 不过在网页端，你知道的，这就很美妙了。

sentences.en: You can just, uh, you know, reserve some space on AWS.
sentences.zh: 你只需要，呃，你知道的，在 AWS 上预留一些空间。

sentences.en: If you're a student, it's free.
sentences.zh: 如果你是学生，这甚至是免费的。

sentences.en: Um, you know, put your, put your site there and other people can interact with it right away.
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道的，把你的网站放上去，其他人马上就能与之互动了。

sentences.en: Um, and so, you know, we're here with Guillermo Rauch, who, who is the creator of Next.js,
sentences.zh: 所以，呃，你知道的，我们今天请到了吉列尔莫·劳赫（Guillermo Rauch），他是 Next.js 的创始人，

sentences.en: which is a platform, um, for basically making that whole process, you know, more beautiful and streamlined.
sentences.zh: Next.js 是一个旨在让整个过程，你知道的，更加美观和简化的平台。

sentences.en: And so I think, um,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，呃……

sentences.en: you know, I think it'd be great for the audience to just kind of get a bit of background on, you know, if someone comes to you not knowing anything about how,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我觉得让观众对背景有个大概了解会很好，如果有人完全不懂前端开发是如何运作的，

sentences.en: how front end dev works, how kind of, can you sort of wrap that up for them?
sentences.zh: 你能不能为他们简要总结一下？

sentences.en: Um, yeah, so that's a good start, you know, front end and back end are kind of the two, uh, divisions that we typically make when you think about how a website works, right?
sentences.zh: 呃，好，这是一个很好的切入点，当你思考网站是如何运作的时候，前端和后端通常是我们划分的两个部分，对吧？

sentences.en: Like front end being the part that your visitors and your users interact with and back end
sentences.zh: 前端就是你的访客和用户进行交互的部分，而后端

sentences.en: being the, uh, systems that support that front end that are typically more related to reading
sentences.zh: 则是支撑前端的系统，通常更多地与从数据库中读取

sentences.en: and writing from databases, uh, talking to other services, talking to other APIs, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 和写入数据、与其它服务通信、与其它 API 通信等等相关。

sentences.en: Um, Next.js is primarily concerned, uh, with the front end and React is primarily concerned with the front end.
sentences.zh: 呃，Next.js 主要关注前端，React 也主要关注前端。

sentences.en: Um, the big thing about React is when we used to make websites in the past, we didn't have good ways of kind of organizing them, um, kind of having the abstractions for making them
sentences.zh: 关于 React，最重要的一点是，当我们过去制作网站时，我们没有好的方法来组织它们，没有很好的抽象机制来让它们

sentences.en: work in ways that were very cohesive.
sentences.zh: 以高度内聚的方式工作。

sentences.en: So React came out of Facebook open source with this idea of websites and web applications are actually made out of components.
sentences.zh: 因此，React 作为开源项目从 Facebook 诞生，其核心理念是：网站和网络应用程序实际上是由组件构成的。

sentences.en: That is to me, the big breakthrough that React has really come up with is this idea that I
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是 React 真正带来的重大突破，也就是我

sentences.en: I've called it in the past Lego blocks for adults.
sentences.zh: 过去称之为“成年人的乐高积木”的理念。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: As you were saying, like when you're starting to create something new, um, you need building blocks, right?
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，当你开始创造新事物时，你需要构建模块，对吧？

sentences.en: Uh, and when you think about front end development, the building blocks that has emerged with, with the rise of React is a component.
sentences.zh: 呃，当你考虑前端开发时，随着 React 的兴起而出现的构建模块就是组件。

sentences.en: So anything that you can, uh, it's funny, like the metaphor, like anything you can build with Legos, right?
sentences.zh: 所以任何你可以……这很有趣，就像那个比喻一样，任何你可以用乐高搭建的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Like you've seen people build all kinds of things, right?
sentences.zh: 就像你见过人们用乐高搭建各种各样的东西，对吧？

sentences.en: From sticking to blocks together to, you know, building, uh, amazing machines.
sentences.zh: 从把积木粘在一起，到，你知道的，建造惊人的机器。

sentences.en: And I think of it that way with React as well, because if you're just new to programming, you can, you know, build a blog.
sentences.zh: 我对 React 的看法也是如此，因为如果你刚接触编程，你完全可以，你知道的，搭建一个博客。

sentences.en: So before we started the call, I was telling you that, uh, when, when we tell people about
sentences.zh: 所以在我们开始通话之前，我跟你说过，呃，当我们告诉人们

sentences.en: learning to make a website with Next.js, we point them to nextjs.org slash learn, and that walks you through creating a blog.
sentences.zh: 如何用 Next.js 学习制作网站时，我们会引导他们访问 nextjs.org/learn，那上面会一步步教你创建一个博客。

sentences.en: And that blog is built with React components.
sentences.zh: 而那个博客就是用 React 组件构建的。

sentences.en: But with, uh, our technology, what we've seen is that people have really built anything you could imagine.
sentences.zh: 但通过我们的技术，我们发现人们实际上已经用它构建了你能想象到的任何东西。

sentences.en: So like Hulu.com, uh, their entire marketing website, but also their viewer for, you know,
sentences.zh: 比如 Hulu.com，他们的整个营销网站，以及当你

sentences.en: when you're watching a show on Hulu online, it's all built with Next.js and React components.
sentences.zh: 在网上看 Hulu 节目时的播放器，全都是用 Next.js 和 React 组件构建的。

sentences.en: So that's awesome.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: It's an incredible technology for, for just organizing this universe that is a front end, um, development workflow.
sentences.zh: 对于组织前端开发工作流这个庞大的宇宙来说，这是一项不可思议的技术。

sentences.en: And one thing, one thing that, that people might not know, I've been getting really, my son's been getting really into Lego.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事，大家可能不知道，我儿子最近对乐高非常痴迷。

sentences.en: And so I've been watching a lot of Lego videos with him.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在陪他看很多乐高视频。

sentences.en: And when they build these huge Lego structures, like if you go to the theme park, right, and there's these enormous Lego, you know, uh, like, like refrigerator sized Lego things is
sentences.zh: 当他们建造这些巨大的乐高建筑时，比如如果你去主题公园，对吧，那里有巨大的乐高，你知道的，像冰箱那么大的乐高模型，

sentences.en: that they actually have something similar.
sentences.zh: 你会发现他们实际上也有类似的做法。

sentences.en: They have this module structure, which is, you know, a group of Legos and they have people kind of just assembling these sort of building blocks.
sentences.zh: 他们有一种模块结构，也就是一组乐高积木，人们只需要把这些积木块组装起来。

sentences.en: And they have other people taking these larger Lego pieces, these modules and sticking them together.
sentences.zh: 还有其他人负责把这些更大的乐高部件、这些模块拼装到一起。

sentences.en: Um, usually it's not just done one Lego at a time.
sentences.zh: 通常不是一次只拼一块乐高。

sentences.en: And so what you're saying is that React and Next let you do that for the web.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，React 和 Next 能让开发者在网页开发中也做到这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's, it's, it's, it really is a good metaphor because, uh, what you're describing is effectively what happens when Next.js developers are building really large things,
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实是一个非常贴切的比喻，因为你所描述的，实际上就是 Next.js 开发者在构建非常宏大的项目时所做的事情，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Like I use Next.js also for my own blog and obviously I just work on it myself.
sentences.zh: 比如我也用 Next.js 来搭建我自己的博客，显然都是我自己一个人在维护。

sentences.en: You know, I, I write about different things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我会在上面写各种内容。

sentences.en: I include components sometimes that are more interactive or sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 有时我会加入一些更具交互性或更复杂的组件。

sentences.en: Uh, like recently I wrote about code golfing and I embedded a code golf demo.
sentences.zh: 比如最近我写了一篇关于代码高尔夫（code golfing）的文章，并在其中嵌入了一个代码高尔夫的演示。

sentences.en: So that's like a really nice property of the web.
sentences.zh: 所以这是网页的一个非常棒的特性。

sentences.en: How, what is code golf?
sentences.zh: 什么是代码高尔夫？

sentences.en: I never heard of this.
sentences.zh: 我从来没听说过这个。

sentences.en: Oh, uh, so code golfing is, uh, basically a competition that happens between developers on who can accomplish a certain outcome or a certain output, usually with the fewest number
sentences.zh: 哦，呃，所以代码高尔夫基本上是开发者之间的一场比赛，看谁能用最少的

sentences.en: of characters.
sentences.zh: 字符来实现某种特定的结果或输出。

sentences.en: Uh, and since we were on the subject of learning to code, I wrote this blog post about, uh,
sentences.zh: 既然我们正在聊学习编程的话题，我写这篇博客就是为了探讨

sentences.en: why code golfing is so great or in general, like little fun competitions are such a great way of learning to code.
sentences.zh: 为什么代码高尔夫如此棒，或者总的来说，为什么这些有趣的小比赛是学习编程的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: And there was this website that I point out called code dash golf.io that basically has this remote verification system to make sure that you give them your program with very few
sentences.zh: 我还在文中指出过一个叫 code dash golf.io 的网站，它基本上有一个远程验证系统，确保你提交的程序使用的字符极少，

sentences.en: characters and they ascertain that, you know, you're getting to the right output and just like golf, you're doing so with the fewest number of strokes, right?
sentences.zh: 并且他们会核实你的程序是否得到了正确的输出，就像打高尔夫球一样，你用最少的击球次数完成任务，对吧？

sentences.en: Oh, that's cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，太酷了。

sentences.en: Oh, now I, now I get the metaphor.
sentences.zh: 哦，现在我懂这个比喻了。

sentences.en: That's awesome.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, so I wrote about it and, um, and yeah, like I said, like my blog is just, you know, uh, not many components and it's for the purpose of just putting some content online.
sentences.zh: 呃，对的，所以我写了关于这个的文章，而且，就像我说的，我的博客很简单，你知道的，没有太多组件，目的只是为了把一些内容放到网上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But when you, when I think about the teams that we support at, at larger enterprises, they are doing exactly what you described.
sentences.zh: 但当你……当我想到我们所支持的大型企业团队时，他们做的事情和你刚才描述的完全一样。

sentences.en: They sometimes have what we call the design systems team where their whole point is to build this, not just now Lego bricks, but you know, you could think of it like stacked
sentences.zh: 他们有时会设立我们所谓的“设计系统团队”，他们的全部意义就在于构建这些——现在不只是乐高积木了，你可以把它想象成堆叠的

sentences.en: Lego bricks or more complex shapes that then their team can reuse.
sentences.zh: 乐高积木或是更复杂的形状，然后他们的团队可以重复使用。

sentences.en: So they're building those modules that you were talking about, almost like, you know, supporting them so that, you know, we know that every website is made out by a series of
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在构建你刚才提到的那些模块，几乎就像是在，你知道的，为团队提供支持，让我们知道每个网站都是由一系列组件组成的，

sentences.en: components that are like buttons and forms and header navigations.
sentences.zh: 比如按钮、表单和头部导航栏。

sentences.en: And so you can sometimes say, okay, I'm going to invest ahead of time in having a team that'll dictate what those reusable larger pieces are.
sentences.zh: 所以有时你可以说，好吧，我要提前投资建立一个团队，由他们来决定这些可复用的更大部件是什么。

sentences.en: And they'll dictate also a visual design language that not only looks like the brand and, and,
sentences.zh: 他们还将规定一种视觉设计语言，这不仅要符合品牌形象，

sentences.en: you know, retains the colors that represent the brand or the system, but also work really well.
sentences.zh: 并保留代表品牌或系统的颜色，还要确保极佳的实用性。

sentences.en: Uh, you know, like the thing about the web and in contrast to, to native mobile development
sentences.zh: 呃，你知道的，网页开发与原生移动开发相比，

sentences.en: is that sometimes it's, it's feels like you're always starting from a scratch that you're always starting from an empty canvas, right?
sentences.zh: 有时感觉你总是从零开始，感觉你总是在一张空白画布上起步，对吧？

sentences.en: Like you, you start at an HTML file and there's nothing there and you've probably seen this, but like the default style sheet of a web browser is just downright gross.
sentences.zh: 比如，你从一个 HTML 文件开始，里面什么都没有，你可能也见过，网页浏览器的默认样式表简直粗糙得不行。

sentences.en: Like, and it's not consistent either.
sentences.zh: 而且它还很不一致。

sentences.en: The text flows from end to end of the screen, which, you know, I'm not an expert in typography,
sentences.zh: 文字会从屏幕的这一端流向另一端，虽然我不是排版方面的专家，

sentences.en: but like, and typesetting, but like, I know that people are not able to read comfortably if text flows from one edge of the screen or the other edge of the screen.
sentences.zh: 但在排版上，我知道如果文字从屏幕的一个边缘一直延伸到另一个边缘，人们是很难舒适阅读的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the web has always felt like this heavy lifting in contrast with like, you know, Apple's design guidelines and their built-in component set.
sentences.zh: 所以相比于苹果的设计指南及其内置的组件库，网页开发总是让人觉得需要做很多沉重的底层工作。

sentences.en: We're like, they've spent, you know, decades thinking about, you know, what makes for a
sentences.zh: 苹果花了数十年时间思考什么才算伟大的用户界面，

sentences.en: great user interface and they give their developers kind of like a lot of preexisting Lego bricks.
sentences.zh: 并为开发者提供了大量现成的乐高积木。

sentences.en: The web, and I think for better is, is a very, um, uh, flexible medium where, you know, you're free to publish anything and you're free to build it however you want.
sentences.zh: 而网页，我认为从好的方面来看，是一个非常灵活的媒介，你可以自由发布任何内容，也可以随心所欲地进行构建。

sentences.en: But in turn, what happens is teams and people tend to have to build their own component systems
sentences.zh: 但反过来，这就导致团队和个人往往不得不构建自己的组件系统，

sentences.en: so that they have this kind of reusable, um, layer and, and that's how they scale their, their companies and their systeMs.
sentences.zh: 以便拥有这种可复用的层，这也是他们扩展公司规模和系统的方式。

sentences.en: And it's been a really nice trend to watch because, you know, at our company, we've built
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的发展趋势，因为在我们公司，我们构建了

sentences.en: our own design system and we, uh, we're putting in constraints in there that are very interesting, for example, for accessibility.
sentences.zh: 自己的设计系统，并且我们在其中设定了一些非常有趣的约束，例如针对无障碍访问（accessibility）。

sentences.en: Like we make sure that our buttons react in certain ways to user input so that, uh, they're accessible
sentences.zh: 比如我们确保我们的按钮对用户的输入做出特定的反应，以便

sentences.en: to people on, you know, screen readers and, and, and things, uh, of that nature.
sentences.zh: 使用屏幕阅读器等辅助设备的用户也能无障碍使用。

sentences.en: And, uh, components can also make sure, you know, that, um, they have the right font sizes
sentences.zh: 而且，组件还可以确保，你知道的，它们拥有正确的字体大小，

sentences.en: so that, you know, the developer doesn't have to come up with a, they don't have to really decide that every time they build something from scratch.
sentences.zh: 这样开发者就不用每次从头构建东西时，都要绞尽脑汁去决定字号。

sentences.en: You're like, what is the right font size for this?
sentences.zh: 你不会去想：这个的正确字号是多少？

sentences.en: What is the right amount of padding for this?
sentences.zh: 这个的正确内边距是多少？

sentences.en: So this has really all been enabled by React creating this idea of you are, as a front end developer, your job is to define components.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切其实都是由 React 创造的理念所赋能的：作为前端开发人员，你的工作就是定义组件。

sentences.en: And, and by doing that, they kind of elevated the abstraction bar because in the past, when
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，他们实际上拔高了抽象的门槛，因为在过去，当你用 JavaScript 编程并从事前端工作时，你所拥有的基元（primitives）

sentences.en: you were programming with JavaScript and you were working on your front end, you had primitives that were, to put it lightly, too primitive.
sentences.zh: 往轻了说，实在是太原始了。

sentences.en: So if you were working with a full stack legacy technology, we're working with templates and
sentences.zh: 如果你使用的是全栈的传统技术，你会使用模板，

sentences.en: then on the client side, you were working with functions or you're working with classes and there was really no structure to how you were doing things.
sentences.zh: 然后在客户端，你使用函数或类，你所做的事情完全没有任何结构可言。

sentences.en: So React came in and we're like, okay, what you're building is not a function per se.
sentences.zh: 所以 React 登场了，它说：好吧，你构建的东西本身不是一个函数，

sentences.en: It's not a class, it's not, you know, a template, it's a component.
sentences.zh: 它不是一个类，它也不是，你知道的，一个模板，它是一个组件。

sentences.en: And by doing that, they've really just revolutionized front end development.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，他们彻底革新了前端开发。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think with, and this might be different with HTML5, you could, you could, you could
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得，虽然这在 HTML5 中可能会有所不同，你可以向我核实这一点，但，

sentences.en: And you know, what's fascinating about this is that we use information about the viewport to prioritize what to prefetch.

sentences.en: So we use, we use an intelligent prioritization system.
sentences.zh: 所以我们使用的是一个智能的优先级系统。

sentences.en: First of all, we prioritize prefetching what's visible on the screen.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们优先预取屏幕上可见的内容。

sentences.en: But secondly, we not, we don't prioritize it so much that it's getting in the way of loading the chessboard, right?

sentences.en: Or whatever it is that then that particular page that you were developing was concerned with rendering.
